name: Swahili
variant: Standard Swahili (Kiswahili sanifu) of Tanzania and Kenya
script: Latin (no extra letters; ng' with an apostrophe), left to right
basis: University of Florida SWA1130 Beginning Swahili syllabus, built on Hinnebusch and Mirza's Kiswahili: Msingi wa Kusema, Kusoma na Kuandika: greetings, -na- present, numbers, negative present, 'to be', -li- past, -ta- future, short verbs, time, object markers, 'to have', locatives
src: University of Florida, SWA1130 Beginning Swahili syllabus (Fall 2021), textbook: Thomas Hinnebusch and Sarah Mirza, Kiswahili: Msingi wa Kusema, Kusoma na Kuandika (2nd ed., 1998)
note: The tense order, numbers, time, object markers, 'to have' and locatives follow the UF schedule. The schedule does not show when each noun class is taught (it only names locative agreement), so the noun-class lessons, their order (M-WA first, then KI-VI, M-MI, JI-MA, N) and the adjective and demonstrative lessons are common course practice and my own judgment. Possessives, question words and the food and shopping lesson are also placed by common practice.
hardest: Noun classes: every noun belongs to a class, and adjectives, verbs and possessives agree with it
Verbs built from prefixes: subject + tense + (object) + root (ni-na-ku-penda)
Negatives that change the prefix and the ending (ninasoma → sisomi)
Swahili time, which counts from 6 a.m. (saa moja = 7 o'clock)

items: Sounds and spelling: five pure vowels, ng', dh, th, gh, and stress on the second-to-last syllable
Greetings: Jambo, Habari?, Shikamoo / Marahaba, Asante
Pronouns and ni / si: mimi ni mwalimu, yeye si mwanafunzi
Commands and the infinitive: soma, someni, kusoma
Numbers 1–100: moja, mbili, kumi, ishirini, mia
Introducing yourself: Jina langu ni…, Ninatoka…, Ninakaa…
Noun classes 1/2 (M-WA): mtu / watu, mtoto / watoto
Question words: nani, nini, wapi, lini, kwa nini, -ngapi
kuwa na: to have (nina, una, sina) and family
Classes 9/10 (N): nyumba, chai, and animals that take M-WA agreement
Adjectives that agree: mtoto mzuri, kitabu kizuri, nyumba nzuri
This and that: huyu, hiki, hii; yule, kile, ile
Telling time the Swahili way (saa moja = 7 o'clock), days and dates
Food and shopping: Bei gani?, shilingi, Naomba…
'To be' in time: nilikuwa, nitakuwa; kulikuwa na
Short verbs that keep ku-: kula, kunywa, kuja (ninakula, nilikunywa)
Places and directions: -ni (sokoni), kushoto, kulia, moja kwa moja
